examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Attributes attach values to grammar nodes. Synthesized attributes depend on children, while inherited attributes may depend on parent or appropriate siblings under the definition. Evaluation order follows a dependency graph; cycles can make a proposed schedule impossible. S-attributed definitions use only synthesized attributes and fit postorder evaluation. Semantic actions placed before or after recursive parsing change output order even when the grammar is unchanged.

**Key relationship:** S-attributed ⊆ L-attributed; evaluate dependencies in topological order

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Write each attribute dependency.
2. Topologically order evaluations.
3. Trace action placement separately from tree structure.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Draw attribute dependencies before choosing an evaluation order. S-attributed definitions contain only synthesized attributes and suit bottom-up evaluation. L-attributed definitions permit inherited attributes from the parent and left siblings under the dependency restrictions. A reference to a right sibling can violate this order or create a cycle.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A production S→AB has B.i=A.s+2 and S.s=A.s+B.s. If A.s=3 and B.s=2B.i, find S.s.

**Answer: 13.** A.s=3 gives B.i=5, then B.s=10. Finally S.s=3+10=13. The left-to-right dependencies can be evaluated without referring to an unevaluated right sibling.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An attribute name such as '.i' does not determine inherited versus synthesized status by itself; its defining production occurrence does.

An attribute dependency cycle prevents a straightforward valid evaluation order.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

An attribute computed only from child attributes is:

- **A.** Always cyclic
- **B.** A lexical state
- **C.** Inherited
- **D.** Synthesized

**Answer: D.** Child-to-parent dataflow defines a synthesized attribute.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** S-attributed definitions use synthesized attributes
- **B.** Attribute dependencies determine valid schedules
- **C.** Semantic action placement cannot change output order
- **D.** Dependency cycles can prevent evaluation

**Answer: A, B, D.** An action before recursion versus after recursion changes when it executes.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

A synthesized rule E.val=E₁.val+T.val has child values 7 and 9. E.val?



**Answer: 16.** Apply the semantic equation after both child values are available: 7+9=16.

#### Pattern 4 · NAT · Transfer problem

Parser production S→aS {print 1} or S→b {print 0}. Parse aaab, then interpret the printed bits as an unsigned binary integer. Value?



**Answer: 7.** The base b prints 0 first. Three pending actions print 1 during unwinding, producing 0111. Its unsigned value is seven.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q60 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/syntax-directed-translation?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Syntax-directed translation and attributes. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. The integer attribute uses I→I1 B with value 2I1.val+B.val, so input 10 has value 2.
2. The fractional attribute for 011 is computed from right to left: F(1)=1/2; F(11)=(1+1/2)/2=3/4; F(011)=(0+3/4)/2=3/8.
3. N.val=2+3/8=**2.375**, within the official interval [2.374,2.376].

#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q29 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/syntax-directed-translation?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Syntax-directed translation and attributes. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. An attribute grammar uses side-effect-free semantic functions, confirming A. Synthesized attributes depend on children and can be evaluated during bottom-up reductions, confirming C.
2. L-attributed definitions admit a depth-first left-to-right evaluation order, so the assertion in B is false.
3. Arbitrary inherited attributes in L-attributed definitions are not automatically implementable during a bottom-up parse merely because the grammar is LR(1); D is false. Select the false statements **B,D**.
